{{Short description|Cryptographic hash function}}
{{More citations needed|date=February 2019}}

In [[cryptography]], '''MDC-2''' ('''Modification Detection Code 2''', sometimes called Meyer–Schilling,{{Citation needed|date=February 2019}} standardized in ISO 10118-2) is a [[cryptographic hash function]]. MDC-2 is a [[One-way compression function|hash function based on a block cipher]] with a proof of security in the ideal-cipher model.<ref>{{cite conference
  | first = John
  | last = Steinberger
  | title = The Collision Intractability of MDC-2 in the Ideal-Cipher Model
  | book-title = Advances in Cryptology – EUROCRYPT 2007
  | pages = 34–51
  | publisher = Springer-Verlag
  | date = June 23, 2007
  | url = http://eprint.iacr.org/2006/294
  | doi = 10.1007/978-3-540-72540-4_3
  | access-date = January 31, 2008| doi-access = free
  | url-access = subscription
  }}</ref> The length of the output hash depends on the underlying block cipher used.

== Algorithm ==
Let <math>E(p,k)</math> be a block cipher encryption function with inputs <math>p</math> (plaintext) and <math>k</math> (key), each of length <math>n</math>, calculating a ciphertext of length also <math>n</math>.
For a given message <math>M</math> to hash, the MDC-2 algorithm proceeds as follows. Let <math>A_1, B_1</math> be two different constants of size <math>n</math>. Let <math>M\, || \, \text{pad} = M_1\,||..||\,M_m</math> where each <math>M_i</math> has size <math>n</math>, then the hash <math>V_m \, || \, W_m</math> of the message is given by:
*for <math>i = 1</math> to <math>m</math>:
**<math>V_i = M_i \oplus E(M_i,A_i)</math>
**<math>W_i = M_i \oplus E(M_i,B_i)</math>
**<math>V_i^L\, || \,V_i^R = V_i</math>
**<math>W_i^L\, || \,W_i^R = W_i</math>
**<math>A_{i+1} = V_i^L\,||\,W_i^R</math>
**<math>B_{i+1} = W_i^L\,||\,V_i^R</math>
*return <math>A_{m+1}\,||\,B_{m+1}</math>.
Here the <math>V_i, W_i</math> are split in halves <math>V_i^L</math> etc., which have the length <math>n/2</math>.

==MDC-2DES hashes==
When MDC-2 uses the [[Data Encryption Standard|DES]] block cipher, the 128-bit (16-byte) MDC-2 hashes are typically represented as 32-digit [[hexadecimal]] numbers. <math>A_1</math> is chosen as the 8-byte string 5252525252525252 and <math>B_1</math> is chosen as the 8-byte string 2525252525252525 (written as hexdigits). Additionally, before each iteration the first byte A[0] of <math>A</math> recalculated as (A[0] & 0x9f) ^ 0x40 and the first byte B[0] of <math>B</math> is recalculated as (B[0] & 0x9f) ^ 0x20.

The following demonstrates a 43-byte [[ASCII]] input (which is padded with five zero-bytes so its length is a multiple of the DES block size of 8 bytes) and the corresponding MDC-2 hash:

  MDC2("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy {{Background color|#87CEEB|d}}og") 
   = 000ed54e093d61679aefbeae05bfe33a

Even a small change in the message will (with probability) result in a completely different hash, e.g. changing <code>d</code> to <code>c</code>:

  MDC2("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy {{Background color|#87CEEB|c}}og") 
   = 775f59f8e51aec29c57ac6ab850d58e8

The hash of the zero-length string is:

  MDC2("") 
   = 52525252525252522525252525252525

==Patent issues==

MDC-2 was covered by {{US patent|4908861}}, issued on March 13, 1990 but filed by [[IBM]] on August 28, 1987. Because of patent concerns support for MDC-2 has been disabled in [[OpenSSL]] on most [[Linux]] distributions and is not implemented by many other cryptographic libraries. It is implemented in [[GNU Privacy Guard|GPG's]] libgcrypt.

The patent was due to expire on August 28, 2007, twenty years after the filing date. It actually expired in 2002<ref>{{Cite journal
  | title = Maintenance Fees for Patent 4,908,861
  | publisher = United States Patent Office
  | date = March 13, 2002
  | url = https://fees.uspto.gov/MaintenanceFees/fees/details?patentNumber=4908861&applicationNumber=07090633
  | website = USPTO Maintenance Fees Site
  | access-date = 2025-09-16
  }}</ref> because IBM did not pay the renewal fee. The Canadian patent was not renewed and no European patent was granted so MDC-2 can now be freely used.
